title: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition: Finance & Legal Guidance 2026
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This guidance document consolidates Redwood Inference’s core Finance and Legal processes for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, procurement and vendor contracting, and revenue recognition/billing policies. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement stakeholders, and business owners who create budget requests, commit to vendor contracts, or own customer billing.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all Redwood Inference business units and legal entities that:
- Request or consume budgeted funds (headcount, infrastructure, marketing, R&D).
- Execute vendor contracts or amendments.
- Submit purchase requests or procurement orders.
- Recognize revenue or issue customer invoices.

This document does NOT replace detailed contract templates or tax advice; refer to Legal for jurisdictional questions and Tax for regulatory treatment.

Ownership and Roles
-------------------
- Finance (FP&A): overall budgeting process, rolling forecast consolidation, P&L ownership, monthly variance reporting.
- Legal: contract templates, negotiation support, risk review, signature authority validation.
- Procurement: vendor onboarding, purchase order (PO) issuance, vendor master data.
- Revenue Operations / Billing: invoice generation, AR aging, revenue journal entries, contract-to-revenue mapping.
- Business Owner: budget owner responsible for request accuracy and approvals.

Key Contact Matrix
- Finance lead (FP&A): Maya Chen, fpanda@redwood.ai
- Legal counsel (Commercial): Omar Patel, legal-comms@redwood.ai
- Procurement manager: Lena Rodriguez, procurement@redwood.ai
- RevRec / Billing owner: Priya Verma, revrec@redwood.ai

Budgeting and Forecasting Process
--------------------------------
Purpose: align annual plan with strategic priorities and produce a rolling 12-month forecast updated monthly.

Annual Budget Cycle (high level):
1. Planning kickoff (Sep): Finance issues guidance (headcount, cost-of-goods, capital thresholds, foreign exchange assumptions).
2. Department submissions (Oct–Nov): business owners upload line-item budgets into the planning tool using standardized templates.
3. Consolidation & review (Dec): FP&A consolidates, performs scenario modeling, and identifies required trade-offs.
4. Executive review & approval (Jan): final budget approved by CFO/CEO and board as required.
5. Communication & allocation (Feb): budgets published to owners and applied to systems.

Rolling Forecast and Monthly Close:
- Forecast cadence: monthly rolling 12-month forecast, with a deeper reforecast each quarter.
- Required inputs: updated hiring plan, MRR/ARR changes, committed contracts, cloud/infrastructure spend, one-time project costs.
- Thresholds: any variance > 10% on a line item vs. prior forecast must include a written remediation plan.

Budget Templates & Controls:
- Standard templates: headcount template (FTE, grade, start date, cost), OpEx template (monthly phasing), CapEx request form.
- Approval matrix:
  - <= $10k: Department head sign-off
  - $10k–$100k: Finance manager + Department head
  - > $100k: VP + Finance Director approval
  - Capital expenditures > $250k: Exec committee review
- All budget changes must have business justification and link to OKRs or project IDs.

Contracts and Legal Process
---------------------------
Purpose: standardize contract lifecycle from request to signature, reduce legal risk, and ensure compliance with approved terms.

Standard Contract Workflow:
1. Request: Business owner initiates contract request in Contract Intake (Confluence form + contract intake ticket).
2. Pre-Review: Procurement validates vendor master data; Legal performs risk-tier classification (low/medium/high).
3. Negotiation: Legal leads negotiation for high-risk clauses (IP, data protection, liability, indemnity, termination, export controls).
4. Commercial Review: Finance validates commercial terms (pricing, taxes, payment terms, credits).
5. Signature: Only authorized signatories may execute contracts. See signature authority matrix below.
6. Post-Signature: Procurement creates PO (if required), Vendor onboarding completes (W-9/Tax, bank details), Contract uploaded to central repository (DocuShare ID).

Signature Authority Matrix (examples):
- Manager level: non-binding NDAs and low-dollar procurement (< $10k) where permitted.
- Director/VP: contracts up to $250k with standard terms.
- CFO/CEO: contracts > $250k or material commercial obligations.

Contract Risk Tiers & Standard Clauses:
- Low risk: standard SaaS terms, no data transfer, standard liability caps (company value-based).
- Medium risk: limited data processing, localized data residency clauses, negotiated SLA credits.
- High risk: source code escrow, material IP assignments, cross-border data transfers, extended indemnities — requires legal director and CISO review.

Procurement Procedures
----------------------
Purpose: efficient vendor selection and purchase execution while maintaining controls and cost discipline.

Procurement Steps:
1. Requisition: Business owner completes a purchase requisition (PR) with justification, cost center, GL codes, and vendor.
2. Approval: PR routed through the approval matrix (see Budgeting section for thresholds).
3. Sourcing: For one-off or > $50k purchases, Procurement obtains at least three quotes unless an approved sole-source rationale exists.
4. PO Issuance: Upon approval, Procurement issues a PO referencing the contract and sends to vendor.
5. Receipt & Invoice Matching: Receiver confirms goods/services delivered. AP matches invoice to PO and receiving confirmation.
6. Payment: AP executes payment per terms; payment methods logged in vendor master.

Vendor Onboarding Checklist:
- Completed vendor master form
- Tax forms (W-9 / W-8BEN as applicable)
- Bank account verification (ACH or wire)
- Insurance certificates where required
- Data processing addendum (DPA) for vendors processing PII or customer data

Procurement Exceptions:
- Emergency purchases: must be escalated to Procurement lead and logged; retrospective approvals required within 5 business days.
- Sole source justification: documented and approved by Procurement Director.

Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
-------------------------------------
Purpose: ensure revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606 (or local equivalent) and billing is accurate and timely.

High-level principles:
1. Identify contract(s) with a customer.
2. Identify performance obligations.
3. Determine the transaction price.
4. Allocate the transaction price to performance obligations.
5. Recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.

Common Redwood Scenarios:
- Hosted API (usage billing): Revenue recognized ratably as usage is delivered. Monthly invoicing with net 30 terms unless otherwise agreed.
- Dedicated/Reserved capacity: For committed monthly/annual contracts, recognize revenue over the committed service period; upfront prepayments are recorded as deferred revenue and amortized.
- Implementation services: Recognize as services are performed (time-and-materials) or per milestone if contract specifies distinct deliverables.
- Term licenses (rare): Amortize over license term if distinct; otherwise follow bundled treatment with services.

Billing Operations:
- Billing cadence: monthly for SaaS/usage, milestone-based for large professional services, or as negotiated per contract.
- Invoice contents: customer name, contract ID, billing period, usage detail (tokens/embedding units), pricing rates, applicable taxes, currency, payment instructions, arrears/credits.
- Dispute handling: customers must notify billing@redwood.ai within 30 days of invoice date to dispute; disputes trigger a billing hold and a 14-day investigation SLA.

Revenue Close Controls:
- Deferred revenue schedule maintained in ERP with linkage to contracts (contract ID).
- Monthly RevRec journal entries reviewed and approved by RevRec owner.
- Any manual adjustments > $10k require Finance Director approval and supporting documentation.

Tax and Compliance Notes:
- Sales/use tax: Billing team coordinates with Tax to determine taxability by jurisdiction.
- Transfer pricing and intercompany: For cross-entity contracts, pricing must follow intercompany policy and be documented.

Reporting and KPIs
------------------
Key metrics tracked monthly:
- Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) and MRR movements
- Deferred revenue balance and burn rate
- Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) — target <= 45 days
- Forecast accuracy: variance between forecasted vs. actual revenue (target <= 5% on rolling 12 months)
- Budget variance: Net operating expense variance (target <= 7%)

Operational Playbooks and Templates
----------------------------------
Included/linked templates (appendix):
- Budget template (headcount, OpEx, CapEx) — attach in Planning tool
- Purchase requisition form (PR template)
- Standard Vendor Contract template (SaaS)
- DPA template for vendors processing Redwood customer data
- Invoice template and sample usage detail export

Appendix A — Approval Matrices (quick reference)
- See Budgeting and Contracts sections for full thresholds.

Appendix B — Sample Contract Intake Checklist
1. Business justification and scope of work
2. Contract term and renewal mechanics
3. Pricing, discounts, and billing cadence
4. Data classification and DPA requirement
5. SLA and credits (if applicable)
6. Termination rights and notice periods
7. Signature authority confirmation
